newsitem.title: USA: Packard Bell NEC to use Robotics 56K modems.
newsitem.headline: Packard Bell NEC to use Robotics 56K modems.

text.p: Packard Bell NEC Inc, U.S. Robotics Corp and Texas Instruments Inc said Thursday the computer maker planned to build new higher speed modems in future Packard Bell and NEC brand computers.

U.S. Robotics' x2 technology, built into modem chipsets manufactured by Texas Instruments, are expected to be available Packard Bell and NEC brand PCs in the second quarter of this year, the companies said.
Packard Bell NEC is the second-largest supplier of personal computers in the United States and the No. 3 supplier worldwide.

The 56-kilobit modem technology would roughly double the speed of the current generation of modems which typically can transfer data at speed of only up to 28,800 bits per second over conventional phone lines.
The Robotics/Texas Instruments faces competition from a second camp led by modem makers Rockwell International Corp, Lucent Technologies Inc and Motorola Inc.

Last week, the latter group joined in forming a coalition of 28 computer and communications equipment makers to develop an industry standard to ensure compatability among 56-kilobit modems. The first meeting is slated for the week of March 20.
Robotics, which announced plans to merge with 3Com Corp Feb. 26, has not said whether it plans to join the coalition.
NEC Corp is a minority stakeholder in closely held Packard Bell NEC Inc.
